ci: benchmark history on GitHub Pages, 2% regression alerts (#194)

* ci: benchmark history on GitHub Pages, 2% regression alerts

- test/embedded/bench_report.h: benchReport() prints one machine-readable
  line per result, BENCH|<name>|<value>|<unit>; the datalog, mult_asm and
  fastdivision benchmarks report their 19 results so (cycles, or us for
  the micros() based ones). simavr is cycle-accurate: the values are the
  same from run to run (checked), only code changes move them.
- scripts/ci/bench_to_json.py: these lines as JSON for
  benchmark-action/github-action-benchmark (customSmallerIsBetter); fails
  on no result or a name reported twice.
- build.yml: the embedded tests run verbose and upload their results
  (also shown in the job summary); every build uploads its flash and RAM.
  A new benchmarks job, the only writer to gh-pages: a push to dev adds a
  point to the history (gh-pages/bench, charts at /bench/); a pull
  request is compared with the last point, and anything more than 2%
  worse gets a comment (not from forks, read-only token). No failure.
- doxygen-gh-pages.yml: the steps of DenverCoder1's action written out,
  since its deploy cleans every file it did not generate; clean-exclude
  keeps bench/. Both jobs share the gh-pages concurrency group.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): the size benchmark reuses the gh-pages branch of the speed one

The Speed step commits its result on the local gh-pages branch (pushed on
dev only); the Firmware size step then fetched gh-pages:gh-pages again,
which git rejects as non-fast-forward. skip-fetch-gh-pages: the branch is
already up to date (on dev, the Speed step has just pushed it, and the
gh-pages concurrency group keeps other writers out).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: performance and size report on every pull request (#195)

* ci: performance and size report on every pull request

As ESPHome does for memory: one comment per pull request, updated at
each push, comparing the target branch with the PR (merged into it, as
CI builds it):

- baseline job: checks out the target branch at base.sha next to the PR,
  and measures it with the PR's scripts/ci/measure.sh (the target may
  predate it): the builds of the build matrix, and the BENCH| results of
  the embedded tests;
- pr-report job: scripts/ci/pr_report.py compares these figures with the
  PR's (the artifacts of the build and test-embedded jobs): flash and RAM
  of every build, the changed benchmarks (all of them folded), ESPHome's
  marks (📈 🚨 beyond 2% worse, 📈 🔸 below, 📉 ✅ / 🎉 better), new and
  removed results. Job summary always; the comment, found by its hidden
  marker and edited in place, unless the PR comes from a fork. A failed
  baseline still gives a report, with the PR's figures alone.
- the history job (gh-pages) now runs on pushes to dev only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(build): branch and commit in the firmware on Linux too

inject_sketch_name.py called git with shell=True and a list of
arguments: on Linux, that only runs the first element, a bare 'git',
which fails - Linux builds (CI included) always said N/A for the branch
and the commit. git now runs without a shell, in the project directory,
and any failure or empty output gives N/A (no git, not a repository,
detached HEAD as in CI checkouts). The hash has a fixed length
(--short=8), so that the firmware size does not move with it: the PR
report compares sizes to the byte.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): measure.sh keeps pio's output out of the JSON

On a fresh runner, pio prints its package installs on stdout, which
measure() pipes into jq: the baseline failed with a jq parse error.
pio's output now goes to stderr.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci(sim): spread the simulation scenarios over parallel jobs (#198)

The grid simulation ran its 13 scenarios in one job, the relay one its 6
long scenarios (330-425 s simulated each) in another: two waves on the 4
vCPUs of a runner, 2-3.5 and 4-6 minutes.

- sim/ci_targets.sh: the make targets of job k of n, from the scenarios on

  scenario runs on its three boards in the same job, which compares them.
- build.yml: grid-sim is a matrix of 4 jobs, one grid scenario each on the
  three boards, and the RF scenarios.
- relay-sim.yml: a matrix of 3 jobs, two relay scenarios each.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(configurator): fallback AP SSID cut to 32 bytes in UTF-8, not 32 characters (#207)

ESPHome 2026.11.0 rejects an access point SSID above 32 bytes, which
broke the "Check the mk2Wifi YAML" step on every PR. The generated SSID
was cut with String.slice(0, 32), which counts UTF-16 units: in French,
"Mk2PVRouter Point d’accès de sec" is 32 characters but 35 bytes ('’' is
3 bytes, 'è' 2).

ssid() now cuts on whole characters to at most 32 bytes, and trims a
trailing space. New test: French and English defaults, long and
multi-byte friendly names all stay within 32 bytes; it fails on the old
code with the CI symptom. Checked with ESPHome 2026.11.0: the three
mk2Wifi presets are valid.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: DC offset refresh without a 15-turn shift loop (#206)

i_DCoffset_V[phase] = l_filterDC_V[phase] >> 15 compiled to a loop of
15 x lsr/ror/ror/ror/dec/brne (~105 cycles), three times per mains
cycle in the ADC ISR. (uint16_t)((l << 1) >> 16) gives bits 15..30 of
the integrator too - '<< 1' only drops bit 31, which the uint16_t drops
as well - in 4 cycles (add/adc/adc/adc).

- identical for all 2^32 values of the uint32_t integrator (checked
  exhaustively on the host)
- grid simulator: ISR average 350.2 -> 348.6 cycles, maxima unchanged
  (the longest calls are not the negative half-cycle ones); all
  expectations pass
- flash -6 B

The simulator's switching events move slightly, as for any ISR timing
change: dev with 8 nops added at the same place (same arithmetic)
diverges from dev at the same event.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(rf): remote loads wait for a working RF module (#204)

If the RFM69 failed to start (missing, unpowered or badly wired),
processRemoteLoadTransmissions() still called radio().send(). The
library then waits up to 1 s for a free channel on every send, and in
sendFrame() forever for "mode ready" / "packet sent" when the module
holds MISO low: the main loop hangs (relays, overrides, dual tariff,
telemetry stop; the ISR keeps routing the local loads).

- remote loads send nothing while SharedRF::initialized is false; their
  payloads stay pending and go out once the module is up
- sendResults() retries initialize_rf() once per datalog period whenever
  an RF chip is configured (before, only with RF logging), and
  send_rf_data() just checks the flag, so a failing module costs one
  ~50 ms retry per period
- simulator: 'rf_absent' scenario command (the router's RFM69 answers
  0 to every SPI read) and scenarios/rf/rf_absent.scn: the override pin,
  read by the main loop, must still force the local loads. dev fails it
  (3/5), this branch passes (5/5); the other RF scenarios pass on both

basic firmware unchanged (byte-identical but for the build timestamp),
rf firmware +16 B.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: energy bucket rounding without the long shift loop (#208)

* perf: energy bucket rounding without the long shift loop

contribution() rounded with (product + 2^(r-1)) >> r, r = shift - 12 (11
for the new board with 50 A CTs, 13 for the old board). avr-gcc -Os
compiles that 32-bit shift into an r-turn loop, three times per mains
cycle in the ADC ISR, including in its longest call.

From r = 9 on, the rounding constant is a multiple of 256, so the same
value is ((product >> 8) + 2^(r-9)) >> (r-8): '>> 8' is a byte move and
the add in between keeps the compiler from merging both shifts again
(3 turns instead of 11). Below 9 (calibrations near the limit of 8), the
general form stays. shift is a constant at the call site in the ISR, so
only one branch is compiled there.

- identical on every reachable input. Exhaustively over all 2^32 values
  of product, for r = 9..16, the forms only differ where the 32-bit add
  of the general form wraps, unreachable since product <= 2^32 - 2^16;
  the new form cannot overflow
- new native test: contribution() equals the general rounding (in 64
  bits) for r = 5..16 (both branches), at the rounding edges and on
  20,000 random (power, calFixed) pairs per r
- grid simulator: longest steady-state ISR call 1,043-1,054 -> 992-1,003
  cycles, one-off start-up maximum 1,395-1,407 -> 1,344-1,356, average
  -0.8; all expectations pass
- flash +10 B

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(sim): 20 A board comparison within 0.1 Wh, like the others

compare-boards-20 allowed 0.05 Wh. A change of ISR timing alone shifts the
switching instants: with the faster energy bucket rounding, surplus_step on
the old board went from 7.14 to 7.22 Wh of grid import with an identical
result of every computation, and the 20 A run ended 0.09 Wh away from it.
0.1 Wh, as for the two other comparisons, stays above that noise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(sim): regulation checked against theory, same code same result (#210)

* test(sim): regulation checked against theory, same code same result

The grid-average windows allowed -120..+80 W (clouds -150..+100) around an
ideal of -20 W, REQUIRED_EXPORT_IN_WATTS: a regulation off by 50 W passed.
Now -30..-10 W in surplus_step and remote_step, -35..-5 W in clouds (its
second window starts 2 s after a step). One mains cycle of a 2 kW load is
40 J, about 3 W over a window. Measured on dev, the #208 and #209 code,
old board and new board with 50 A and 20 A CTs: -13.1 to -25.1 W.

The firmware prints its banner at 9600 baud before it samples, so the
banner's length shifts the run against the scenario: the same #209 code
gave 7.20 Wh of grid import in surplus_step from a branch, 7.15 Wh from a
detached HEAD (CI). With PVR_SIM_BUILD set, the build writes the branch
name a CI checkout gives (N/A); the grid simulation workflows set it.
From a branch and from a detached HEAD, the summaries are now identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(sim): random RF losses at most 3 in a row in lossy_link

lossy_link loses 10 % of the frames at random, from a fixed sequence
drawn frame after frame. Which frames the sequence falls on depends on the
firmware's timing: with #209, the frames go out in a slightly different
order at start-up, and node 15 lost 4 frames in a row, a 0.503 s gap
against the receiver's 0.5 s timeout - one link loss, against none
expected. At 10 %, a few runs in a hundred have such a run, whatever the
code.

rf_loss takes an optional limit on the losses in a row, per node; the
sequence itself is unchanged. lossy_link uses 3: the receivers must keep
their loads through 3 frames lost in a row, which the scenario meant.

Dev and #209 (merged with dev): check-rf 41/41.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: load states from a mask table, updatePhysicalLoadStates not inlined (#209)

* perf: load states from a mask table, updatePhysicalLoadStates not inlined

updatePhysicalLoadStates() tested each load's override by shifting the
16-bit override bitmask by its pin, an n-turn loop on AVR (~100 cycles per
mains cycle with pins 5-7), counted a remote load's ordinal with a loop
over the map, and re-read the volatile bitmask for every load.

- Load::overrideMasks() builds, at compile time and in flash, the bit of
  each load in the local or the remote override bitmask; the loop tests a
  mask, and reads the bitmasks once per cycle.
- updatePhysicalLoadStates() is a real call instead of always_inline:
  inlined, it takes registers that the rest of the ISR spills to a 6-byte
  stack frame on every call. As a call, the ISR has no stack frame.

Grid simulator, basic firmware (old board), against dev:
- average ISR call 348.6-348.8 -> 318.8-318.9 cycles
- longest steady-state call 1,043-1,054 -> 978-989
- one-off start-up maximum 1,395-1,407 -> 1,329-1,341
- RF build with remote loads: average 359.3-359.7 -> 351.3-351.7, maximum
  1,409 -> 1,399
- flash 8,512 -> 8,418 B, initialised RAM 58 -> 54 B
- all expectations pass (30 basic, 36 RF)

The table alone, with the function still inlined, is slower (+2 cycles on
average): the gain comes from the call. The other forced-inline functions
were tried one by one; none improves both the average and the maximum.

Native tests for the masks (195/195). ISR figures updated in CLAUDE.md,
architecture.md and performance.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: ISR figures with #208 merged

Measured on this branch merged with dev (#204, #208), against dev:
- average ISR call 347.8-348.0 -> 318.0-318.1 cycles
- longest steady-state call 992-1,003 -> 925-936
- one-off start-up maximum 1,332-1,350 -> 1,270-1,285
- flash 8,524 -> 8,426 B, initialised RAM 58 -> 54 B

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: no optimize("-O3") on the functions inlined into the ISR (#211)

nextLogicalLoadToBeAdded(), nextLogicalLoadToBeRemoved() and
processDataLogging() are always_inline: their code is compiled with the
options of the ISR they land in, so the attribute did nothing. Without it,
the firmware is the same to the byte (basic, and rf with remote loads,
build strings frozen).

The attribute stays where the function is a call of its own, with what it
is worth noted next to it:
- updatePortsStates(): -O3 unrolls the load loop into constant masks; with
  -Os, the ISR takes 38 cycles more on average and 88 more at most
  (grid simulator, surplus_step)
- initializeProcessing(): 50 bytes smaller with -O3 than with -Os

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: a change of one micros() step is no change in the PR report (#213)

The microsecond benchmarks time a loop with micros(), which counts in
steps of 4 us at 16 MHz. When the code before the loop moves by a few
cycles, the same loop reads one step more or less: #212 got "slightly
worse" for multU16x16_to32 (+4 us on 127,608 us), with a loop identical
to the instruction, and -4 us on mult16x8_q8.

The report now counts a change within one step of its unit (4 us) as no
change, and says so in the change column. Results in cycles (Timer1,
interrupts off) are unchanged: exact to the cycle. Footer and test README
explain it.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

build: link with --relax, also suggested for the Arduino IDE (#212)

The compiler emits every call and jump to another function in its long,
absolute form (call/jmp, 4 bytes), since final addresses are only known
at link time. With --relax, the linker turns each one whose target is
within 4 KB into the relative form (rcall/rjmp, 2 bytes, one cycle less)
and moves everything after it.

- flash 8,422 -> 8,152 B (default build, build strings frozen); 127 of
  184 calls become rcall
- the vector table keeps its 4-byte slots (rjmp + nop): every vector at
  the same address, one cycle less to enter an interrupt
- ADC ISR: average 318.0 -> 317.0 cycles, maximum -1 to -5: the ISR is
  inlined, the vector is its only frequent jump
- grid simulator, 3 boards, relays, RF: 190/190 expectations, boards
  compare the same; embedded tests (simavr, built with it): 113/113

The READMEs suggest the same flag in platform.txt to Arduino IDE users.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: configuration checks that let wrong settings through, or reject good ones (#214)

validation.h, load_map.h:
- Load::remote() with a unit outside 1..3 packed as another unit: unit 4
  wrapped to 0, so remote(4, 8) became a local load with its TRIAC on the
  LED pin. remote() now returns a marker entry, reported by
  Load::hasValidRemoteUnits() with one error of its own; the other checks
  skip it, so no cascade.
- "Duplicate pin definition" for a router whose loads are all remote, with
  no other pin: check_pins() returned the pins used, 0 also meaning a
  conflict. It now returns { unique, used }.
- A REMOTE_LOAD(n) override target beyond NO_OF_REMOTE_LOADS forced
  nothing, silently (REMOTE_LOAD counts from 0); now an error. Skipped when
  the load map itself is invalid, which has its own error.
- ROTATION_AFTER_SECONDS is compared with a 16-bit counter of seconds: at
  most 65534 s (about 18 h), not 24 h.
- With relays, RELAY_FILTER_DELAY must span at least 5 datalog periods:
  below, the triple EMA of the filter shifts by a negative count.
- dualtariff.h: OffPeakDuration * 3600U, unsigned like its result.

configurator: the same rotation limit (18 h) and relay filter check, in
English and French, with tests.

Checked: wrong units 0 and 4 (with and without LED) give one error;
all-remote maps build; real duplicates, RX/TX pins and REMOTE_LOAD(n) off
by one are reported; native 197/197, rf build with remote loads,
configurator 110/110.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: every benchmark in exact CPU cycles, reported in us and cycles (#215)

The loop benchmarks (mult_asm, fastdivision) timed with micros(): steps of
4 us, plus every millis() interrupt in between, so a result moved by one
step when unrelated code moved. They now count cycles with Timer1 extended
to 32 bits by its overflow interrupt (bench_timer.h), millis() paused and
the serial output sent first: exact and independent of where the loop
starts.

Every result is reported twice, `<name> [us]` (cycles / 16, exact to
1/16 us) and `<name> [cycles]`, including the datalog math results that
were in cycles only.

The PR report drops the one-step rule of #213, now unneeded, and shows up
to 4 decimals.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: speed charts on GitHub Pages, one small chart per benchmark (#216)

* ci: speed charts on GitHub Pages, one small chart per benchmark

Each push to dev adds the embedded benchmarks to bench/history.json,
next to the sizes: {name: cycles}, from the "[cycles]" results of the
test-embedded job (the "[us]" ones are cycles / 16, shown by the page).

The page gets a Speed section: small multiples grouped by test suite,
each with its own scale (from 156 to 12.6 million cycles), the latest
value in cycles and us, a tooltip per commit and a table per suite.

The pages job now waits for test-embedded too; failed embedded tests do
not hold back the sizes, the entry then has no speed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: loop benchmarks report one operation, in cycles and us

The loop benchmarks reported the whole loop: 1,573,974 cycles for
multS16x16_to32 are 36,000 multiplications, 43.7 cycles each. They now
report one operation (loop overhead included), with a name saying so:
"... per op", "... per call", "... per sample". benchCycles() takes the
number of operations: the cycles get two decimals, the us stay at four.

The human-readable output gives cycles and us per operation too
(printPerOp), and the history on Pages keeps the decimals.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: one row per benchmark in the PR report, with us and cycles columns

The speed table of the PR report had two rows per function, its "[us]"
and "[cycles]" results. It now has one: us and cycles of the target
branch and of the PR side by side, and the change, computed on the
cycles (the exact figure). The step summary of the embedded tests gets
the same layout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
